newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian secret police chief resigns - premier.
newsitem.headline: Albanian secret police chief resigns - premier.

text.p: Albania's new Prime Minister Bashkim Fino announced on Friday that the head of the secret police had resigned and the widely-feared force would be controlled by the government rather than the president.

Fino, in his first news conference since being appointed earlier this week, also said parliament was considering a proposal to lift press censorship imposed as part of a state of emergency two weeks ago.

The resignation of Bashkim Gazidede, head of the sinister leather-jacketed Shik secret police, was one of the main demands of anti-government rebels who seized most of southern Albania at the outbreak of unrest which has engulfed the whole country.
Fino said parliament was poised to approve an order putting the Shik under the control of the Defence and Interior ministries. At present it is directly controlled by the president, Sali Berisha.
Fino said he had discussed with European mediator Franz Vranitzky earlier on Friday the possible creation of an international force to help restore order in the country.
But he expressed the hope that Albanians themselves would succeed in restoring the rule of law, and that such a force would not be necessary.
